newsitem.title: ESTONIA: PRIVATISATION VOUCHERS TRADED ON FREE MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATISATION VOUCHERS TRADED ON FREE MARKET.

text.p: Privatisation vouchers (EVPs) can from Monday be traded on the free market of the Estonian bourse, a listing seen helping their liquidity, analysts said.
They added that they expected the vouchers to remain volatile in price.
Privatisation vouchers or EVPs were handed out to the public to allow people to take part in the privatisation of state-owned companies that were nationalised during the Soviet era.
"The listing is expected to stabilise the price and make the spread smaller," Sander Danil, analyst from Tallinna Pank said.
"There was always a wide spread between the bid and ask price and the listing should narrow this somewhat," said Katrin Kaarli, analyst with Hansapank.
"The voucher should become more liquid after listing as well as the previous system was rather complicated," she added.
The vouchers were previously traded in the central depository of securities and held in special bank accounts.
EVPs are expected to be in demand in the future before the privatistion of remaining large state enterprises.
"Trading in EVPs should be more active before the sale of a stake in a larger enterprise like Eesti Gaas, but for the most part I think they should be quite," Danil added.
The privatisation agency said it will sell off part of the government stake in Eesti Gaas for privatisation vouchers.
